ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates; screening against UN Security Council sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, and domestic Cypriot sanctions lists; mandatory OFAC-style screening when operating in international banking corridors. A risk-based AML/CFT approach must be documented and approved by senior management.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRC) – Online Companies Portal (companies.gov.cy)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in Greek or English/Latin characters. If the chosen name is in Greek, an official English transliteration must be filed to ensure consistency in EU and international registries. A private limited company name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may request written reasons, file a reconsideration request with the DRC within 14 days, and if refused, lodge an administrative recourse before the Cypriot Administrative Court under Article 146 of the Constitution within 75 days of notification. If rejection is due to similarity with an existing name, the applicant may submit written consent from the registered owner or amend the proposed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the operational inflight catering facility. A non-operational registered office address is permitted for general correspondence, but the physical catering kitchen and ramp delivery facility must be established and licensed in Cyprus.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk; conservatively 75% probability of unannounced on-site inspections in the first year due to mandatory food safety licensing by the Cyprus food safety authority and Cyprus Civil Aviation Authority ramp security inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cyprus Companies Act, Cap. 113 (as amended), ss. 4, 6, 56 and 177 read with Table A of the First Schedule
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOROR), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia; Ariadne e-Filing Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation under s. 6 of the Companies Act, Cap. 113, filed together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company limited by shares; shares may be issued unpaid or fully paid in cash or in kind. No escrow or pre-incorporation capital deposit is mandated. A nominal authorised capital of EUR 1,000 is recommended for banking and airport concession purposes; capital duty is effectively 0% and only nominal stamp duty applies on the share capital statement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscription of 1,000 ordinary shares by the founding shareholder is approved and allotted per the Memorandum and Articles of Association, with payment terms as recorded in the allotment statement. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office be established at the address in the Registered Office Notice, which the Directors are authorized to lodge with the Registrar. RESOLVED FURTHER that the persons named in the director acceptance forms are appointed first Directors, with [Name] as Company Secretary, and the Directors are authorized to execute and file corporate, tax, social-insurance and licensing documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search, Reservation and Trade-Name Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOROR), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry — Ariadne e-Filing Portal; District Administration for trade-name registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name-reservation application on the Ariadne portal with two alternative Latin-script names, specifying the legal type 'Private Limited Company'. The Registrar searches against existing HE-registered entities and reserved names, and issues a name-approval certificate. If the commercial brand differs from the corporate name, file a separate trade-name application and obtain the District trade-name certificate to support airport concession and catering documentation.
required_dossiers: Ariadne name reservation application (electronic)
Two proposed corporate names with 'Ltd' suffix
Consent letter from intended directors where personal names are used
Notarized power of attorney appointing the filing agent
Trade-name registration application and fee receipt (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for resemblance to an existing HE registry entry, file a revised name immediately or appeal to the Registrar under s. 25(1) of Cap. 113 within the statutory objection period; re-submit with a new distinguishing element while the reservation file remains open.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Cyprus advocate and notary public; subsequent filing with DRCOROR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct counsel to draft the M&A adopting Table A with private-company modifications, including broad objects covering catering, food manufacture, bonded logistics and airport ramp delivery. Each subscriber executes the M&A before a witness and the documents are notarized. The notary countersigns certified copies for registry filing, and the registered office address is confirmed by a letter of consent from the lessor.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association
Notarized Articles of Association
Subscribers' declaration of intention to form the company
Consent of lessor for registered office address
Notarized power of attorney where incorporation is carried out by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registrar requisitions on defective or ultra vires clauses are cured by filing a supplementary deed of rectification or amended M&A pages, re-executed by subscribers and re-notarized within the prescribed requisition deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Application Filing and Statutory Fee Settlement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DRCOROR — Ariadne e-Filing Portal; head-office counter in Nicosia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the prescribed application for registration of a private company limited by shares, accompanied by the notarized M&A and declarations of consent of the first directors and company secretary. Authorize payment of the statutory incorporation fee and stamp duty from the filing agent's account. The e-submission must be digitally signed by a licensed filing representative; verify the Registrar's acknowledgment receipt and requisition schedule.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of a Private Company (Registrar Form)
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (duplicate)
Consent to act as first director (statutory declaration)
Consent to act as company secretary
Statement of registered office address
Receipt of incorporation fee and stamp duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any requisition items within the Ariadne workflow and re-submit within the curing period of 14 to 30 days; if the file lapses, submit a fresh application while relying on the preserved name reservation if still valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation Issuance and Registry Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful examination, the Registrar enters the company in the HE registry and issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the date of registration. Download the certified registry extract, obtain certified true copies of the M&A, and open the statutory internal records: register of members, register of directors and secretary, and registered office minute book.
required_dossiers: Registrar's registration entry showing the HE number
Certificate of Incorporation (original)
Certified registry extract of first officers and registered office
Company minute book and share certificate templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the certificate or extract contains typographical or registry data-entry errors, apply to the Registrar for administrative rectification without re-filing, returning the original certificate for cancellation and reissue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Filings: First Board Resolutions, Officer Notices and Registered Office Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DRCOROR; company secretary; statutory governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting and adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption and officer appointments. Notify the Registrar of the registered office address and file the return of initial directors and secretary within the prescribed 14-day filing window. Issue share certificates, record allotments in the register of members, and maintain board minutes in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Signed minutes of the first board meeting
Registered office notice (Registrar form)
Return of Directors and Secretary with notarized consents
Share certificates and allotment statements
Register of members entries and beneficial ownership declaration for the UBO register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late statutory returns are cured by filing with explanatory submissions and applicable late fees; if the Registrar refuses late filing, an application may be made to the competent district court for an order extending time under the Companies Act, Cap. 113.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Tax, Employer and Operational Registration Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance (Taxisnet); Social Insurance Services, Ministry of Labour; Health Insurance Organisation; DRCOROR for registry updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company electronically with the Tax Department to obtain the Tax Identification Number (TIN), and apply for VAT registration where projected taxable turnover exceeds EUR 15,600 or where zero-rated bonded catering supplies justify early registration. Register as employer with the Social Insurance Services and the Health Insurance Organisation for GHS contributions. In parallel, open a dedicated corporate bank account, deposit the initial share capital in accordance with the allotment statement, and file the UBO declaration in the company's central beneficial ownership register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Details of directors, secretary and beneficial owners
UBO declaration under the Cyprus AML and central register framework
Lease agreement for registered office
Projected turnover statement for VAT threshold assessment
Bank reference and confirmation of initial capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Delays in TIN or VAT issuance are cured through authorised tax agent follow-up and interim submissions; late VAT registration is regularized by filing a correction notice with the Tax Department and settling any assessed liability, penalties or interest as applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health (Health Services Department, Food Hygiene and Food Safety Units) in conjunction with the State General Laboratory; coordinated at airport level by Hermes Airports Ltd
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operation Approval — Airline Catering Establishment License, issued under Regulation (EC) No. 852/2004 and the national Food Hygiene and Food Safety Laws as amended

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Annex II Project Category — EIA Screening Examination expected; a greenfield kitchen or substantial modification of utilities inside the airport catering unit triggers a preliminary examination opinion, with an environmental site report and waste management notice; a full EIA Report is not anticipated for a HACCP-licensed kitchen on an existing airport plot with sewer connectivity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Kitchen effluent must pass through certified grease interceptors with fats, oils and grease (FOG) not exceeding 100 mg/L where discharged to municipal sewer; BOD5 not exceeding 500 mg/L and COD not exceeding 1000 mg/L per district sewerage board pre-treatment limits; no direct surface-water discharge without an effluent discharge permit. Air extraction systems must conform to the EU BREF on Food, Drink and Milk Industries, covering odour dilution thresholds, VOC abatement through activated carbon or grease filtration, and acoustic limits at the airport boundary. Food waste and used cooking oil (UCO) must be classified and transferred under Law No. 185(I)/2011 to licensed waste carriers with weighbridge dockets and auditable records.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification: fire compartmentation, means-of-escape, suppression system review and annual inspection by the Cyprus Fire Service, including canopy and duct grease-cleaning logbooks and structural load certification for electromechanical kitchen equipment. Occupational clearance: risk-assessment-based certification by the Department of Labour Inspection under the Safety and Health at Work Law (Law 89(I)/1996), covering ventilation, manual handling, first aid, engineering controls and personal health surveillance. Airport-side clearance: restricted-area access and ramp safety authorization from Hermes Airports Ltd and the Aviation Security Directorate of Cyprus Police for catering vehicles and vetted personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Tax Department of the Republic of Cyprus (Τμήμα Φορολογίας), Ministry of Finance; online filing portal: TaxisNet ('Tax for All') at https://taxportal.mof.gov.cy; corporate income tax returns filed via the ARIADNE e-filing system; customs export processing administered by the Department of Customs and Excise (Τμήμα Τελωνείων) through the Cyprus Customs Single Window (EAS/Single Administrative Control System).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Cyprus Ltd: (1) obtain Certificate of Incorporation HE77 from the Registrar of Companies; (2) register for corporate income tax with the District Tax Office using Form TD2001, resulting in an 8-digit Cyprus Tax Identification Code (TIC); the entity is taxable at the 12.5% CIT rate on worldwide income if tax-resident, or on Cyprus-source income/PE profits if non-resident; (3) file Form VAT 101 (Application for VAT Registration) with the VAT Division; non-resident entities must appoint a tax representative in Cyprus under Art. 75 of the VAT Law; (4) obtain an EORI number from the Department of Customs and Excise to move goods under customs control; (5) provide passports of directors/UBOs, certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles of association, registered office address, and bank account evidence; registrations are typically processed within 10-30 business days and tax clearance letters may be requested under airline procurement contracts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope: tax-resident Cyprus Ltd (managed-and-controlled / PoEM test) is taxed on worldwide income at 12.5% CIT; non-resident Ltd is taxed only on Cyprus-source income and profits attributable to a Cyprus permanent establishment; pass-through treatment is not available to Cyprus companies; no tax-exempt zone applies to ISIC 5621 operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus has no US-style check-the-box election; legal form determines tax classification. Available elections: (i) group loss relief election under Art. 26 of the Income Tax Law; (ii) VAT group registration election under Art. 39 of the VAT Law; (iii) intra-Community VAT identification for cross-border EU supplies; (iv) cash-accounting basis for small taxpayers where turnover allows; (v) unilateral foreign tax credit election under Art. 36 ITA; (vi) election between IFRS and Cyprus GAAP for the first tax accounts; (vii) tonnage tax and IP-Box elections exist in Cyprus law but are not applicable to inflight catering (ISIC 5621); (viii) special customs warehousing and excise-suspension arrangements may be elected at the airport bonded kitchen with Customs approval, deferring duty/VAT until goods are uplifted for export.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Cyprus VAT Law No. 95(I)/2000, harmonised with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC; excise duties under the Excise Duties Law N.91(I)/2017 for aviation fuels/imported consumables where applicable; Cyprus imposes no separate GST or sales-and-use tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 of taxable turnover in the preceding or current 12-month period (Art. 30, Cyprus VAT Law); EUR 10,000 for intra-EU distance sales; non-resident suppliers physically supplying goods from Cyprus airside facilities do not benefit from threshold exemption and must register from the first taxable supply because inflight catering invoices typically exceed the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Cyprus does not operate real-time B2B fiscal clearance or digital stamping as of 2025. Mandatory e-invoicing applies to business-to-government (B2G) supplies under the PE-Billing framework implementing EU Directive 2014/55/EU (Cyprus Law N.51(I)/2017), using Peppol BIS v3 / UBL with Cyprus CIUS extensions. Newly registered taxpayers must maintain electronic books using tax-approved software and integrate Electronic Sales Devices (ESD) for declared data transmission to the Tax Department. Intra-Community zero-rated supplies require electronic VIES recapitulative statements. Customs export declarations must be lodged electronically via the Cyprus Customs Single Window (EAS) and cleared before aircraft loading. Cyprus is preparing for EU ViDA digital reporting rules, which will mandate structured e-invoicing for cross-border intra-EU transactions within the 2030 rollout.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero percent VAT applies where the Cyprus caterer supplies inflight meals as provisions of aircraft: (i) exports of goods dispatched outside the EU, zero-rated under Art. 65 of the VAT Law once exportation is evidenced by a Customs export declaration; (ii) supplies of goods for fuelling and provisioning of aircraft operated by airlines on international flights, zero-rated under Art. 66(1) of the VAT Law (including meals and beverage carts laden onto departing aircraft via ramp delivery); (iii) intra-EU B2B supplies to airlines or catering hubs in other member states, zero-rated with a valid EU VAT number, VIES listing and transport documentation; (iv) supplies from a bonded/customs-warehouse kitchen into an aircraft store are deemed exported and zero-rated on exiting the warehouse regime. Zero-rating is conditional on the caterer obtaining conclusive proof of exportation within three months of the supply; failure to obtain such evidence recharacterises the supply as domestic at 19% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / EAS lodged in the Cyprus Customs Single Window)
Commercial Invoice and Inflight Catering Manifest / Commissary Order
Air Waybill / Master Air Waybill with Flight Load Sheet for ramp-delivered meals
Carrier's certificate of loading or Customs-endorsed proof that the goods departed the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (or SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation evidencing settlement from the foreign airline)
Aircraft provisioning certificate where zero-rating is claimed under Art. 66 of the VAT Law
Customs warehouse / airside bonded movement records where meals are held under excise or customs suspension
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to audits by the Cyprus Tax Department, post-clearance integrity checks by the Department of Customs and Excise, and anti-money-laundering reviews against false or circular export documentation. A false export zero-rating claim constitutes VAT fraud under Art. 123 of the VAT Law N.95(I)/2000, attracting penalties of up to twice the tax evaded with minimum per-default fines, statutory late-payment interest, default assessments, confiscation orders, and criminal custodial penalties on indictment. Assessment windows of 5 years (extended to 10 years for fraudulent conduct) permit retrospective clawback of zero-rating, disallowance of input VAT, and surcharges. Directors of the Ltd may be held personally liable for reckless attestations. Where export proceeds are not repatriated or bank evidence of payment is absent, the Tax Department may recharacterise the export as a domestic supply and assess 19% VAT on the full invoice value; Cyprus abolished exchange controls in 2015, so the 180-day benchmark reflects standard export-proceeds evidence integrity and prudential airline credit terms rather than a statutory repatriation requirement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Kentriki Trapeza tis Kyprou), operating within the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) of the European Central Bank. The Central Bank of Cyprus is the competent licensing and prudential supervisor for all Cyprus-incorporated credit institutions, including Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic Bank, Eurobank Cyprus, Alpha Bank Cyprus and AstroBank, and receives mandatory International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) statistical returns from resident banks for balance-of-payments compilation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Cyprus is a Eurozone member state (adopted the euro on 1 January 2008) and therefore applies Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, guaranteeing full freedom of movement of capital. There are no exchange-control restrictions on either current-account transactions (inflight catering imports of food ingredients, packaging, kitchen equipment, aviation services, royalties, salaries, insurance premiums) or capital-account transactions (equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend distributions, license fees, liquidation proceeds, profit repatriation). The euro is unconditionally convertible into all major currencies through the domestic interbank market and through correspondent banks without Central Bank approval or conversion-license requirements. Profit and dividend remittance by a non-resident shareholder of CY_LTD is permitted without prior Central Bank authorization; the only documentary prerequisites are (i) a board resolution approving the distribution, (ii) audited IFRS financial statements evidencing legally distributable reserves under the Cyprus Companies Law Cap.113, (iii) the corporate tax residency certificate (Form T.D. 121) of CY_LTD, and (iv) confirmation of applicable dividend withholding tax treatment under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (where the parent is an EEA resident, withholding is zero). The only frictions to convertibility are (a) mandatory EU/UN sanctions screening and, for US Dollar settlement, OFAC screening by correspondent banks; and (b) post-transaction statistical reporting by the commercial bank to the Central Bank of Cyprus under the ITRS using BPM6 classification codes. No capital-account approval, investment permit, or conversion quota applies to a Cyprus private limited company engaged in ISIC 5621 airport inflight catering.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Cyprus abolished its Exchange Control Law in 1994 and has never reintroduced export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion ratios, repatriation deadlines, or designated-account requirements. All proceeds from exported catering services (inflight meal uplift and ramp-side delivery to foreign air carriers at Larnaca Airport LCA and Paphos Airport PFO) may be freely retained in EUR or any foreign currency in a Cyprus-domiciled multi-currency account at the company's Tier-1 bank, or converted to EUR at commercial interbank rates without Central Bank approval. The only obligations associated with export receipts are (i) correct ITRS inflow classification by the receiving bank (typically BPM6 code USD/SE for services), (ii) retention of SWIFT MT103/SEPA payment confirmations and customs/intrastat documentation for six years under the Cyprus Income Tax Law N.118(I)/2002 audit and anti-avoidance provisions, and (iii) ordinary invoicing and VAT accounting under the Cyprus VAT Law N.95(I)/2000 for the sale of meals and services to airlines (B2B reverse-charge treatment applies for catering supplies). There is no statutory timeline for surrender, no minimum conversion percentage, and no Central Bank of Cyprus monitoring of the commercial disposition of exported proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (EUR) and Operational Multi-Currency Account (EUR/USD/GBP) with SWIFT gpi, SEPA Direct Debit, and Trade Finance (Commercial LC) module
Operational Account (EUR) with Integrated SEPA Credit Transfer, SEPA Direct Debit (Core), Internet Banking Host-to-Host connectivity for Monthly ACH-style batch settlements
Operational Account (EUR) and Multi-Currency Foreign Exchange Account (USD/GBP/CHF) for airline invoicing and FX forward settlements
Operational Account (EUR) with payroll and supplier payment automation, ancillary to the primary banking group
Operational Account (EUR) with integrated airport concession payment facilities for periodic ramp and gate-leasing payments to Hermes Airports Ltd

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury settlement rail; Medium as a segregated auxiliary operating float. Legal framework: EU PSD2 permits Cyprus corporate entities to open payment accounts with licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Revolut Business, Wise Business, Modulr and PPS, passporting e-money licenses into Cyprus from other EEA member states; such EMIs are not credit institutions licensed by the Central Bank of Cyprus and may not provide capital escrow accounts, documentary letters of credit, bank guarantees, or full correspondent-banking treasury services. Operational constraints: (i) inbound 'Aviation Contract Wire' remittances from foreign airlines are commonly routed through the EMI's own settlement bank and are subject to enhanced counterparty vetting, creating operational friction and possible rejection when the remitter (a non-EEA air carrier) sees an EMI IBAN; (ii) the 'Monthly ACH' settlement schedule (in EU terms SEPA Direct Debit Core) functions smoothly from an EMI, but the underlying commercial supply contract and trade finance arrangements require a full-bank operating account; (iii) high-velocity flows between an EMI wallet and a Cyprus Tier-1 bank, without a documented service contract, are treated by Cyprus AML compliance as a suspicious-flow trigger; and (iv) group-level CySEC-licensed affiliates (where applicable) face additional de-risking because compliance departments disfavor concentration of group treasury in single e-money wallets. The prescribed design is therefore: use a fintech EMI exclusively for corporate card expenditure and deniable petty-cash kitchen purchases, never for airline receivables, capital injections, or commercial LC settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is strongly recommended and is, in practice, effectively mandatory for non-EEA resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs). The Cyprus AML legal framework (Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Activities Law N.188(I)/2007, as amended) does not contain an express statutory right to fully remote onboarding; each licensed bank applies its own risk-based KYC policy. Current Q4-2025 market practice: for directors and UBOs residing in the EU/EEA, Bank of Cyprus and Hellenic Bank accept qualified video-identity onboarding (notarized apostilled identity documents pre-validated through the bank's secure portal, followed by a live video call with the compliance officer); for non-EEA resident directors or UBOs, and for any beneficial owner resident in a non-FATF or high-risk third country, an in-branch compliance interview at the bank's Nicosia or Limassol headquarters is uniformly required and should be booked between 5 and 10 business days after submission of the digital KYC packet. Given the statutory catering license requirements under the Cyprus Food Law (N.54(I)/2005) and Regulation (EC) 852/2004, the onboarded director must demonstrate the ability to supervise the Larnaca airport bonded food-production unit; the most time-efficient mechanism is alignment of the bank's physical KYC interview with the same business trip in which the local food-safety officer and the Veterinary Services and Food Safety Directorate inspection are conducted. Document signing may be executed through a Cyprus-licensed lawyer with a power of attorney, but the interview itself cannot ordinarily be delegated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) verification and Cyprus Beneficial Ownership Register compliance: banks will not commence onboarding until the Cyprus Registrar of Companies Beneficial Ownership Register extract for CY_LTD is submitted, and will reject any structure with nominee layers, bearer shares, or undisclosed indirect ownership above 25%.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Official Beneficial Ownership Register extract of CY_LTD issued by the Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver dated within 7 business days of application; (2) group organizational chart signed by a director, disclosing each natural-person UBO with Nature of Control (direct/indirect, voting rights or ownership); (3) certified share certificates and register of members of CY_LTD; (4) for any corporate UBO, its official trade-registry extract and EEA UBO-registry excerpt (where applicable); (5) apostilled passports of all natural-person UBOs; (6) an AML declaration letter under N.188(I)/2007 confirming no nominee arrangement and no bearer instruments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth for the initial equity injection: even a low-nominal Cyprus Ltd capital contribution raises suspicion when the funding originates from a high-velocity personal account, from a non-EEA jurisdiction, or in a lump sum without an economic narrative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Three full months of remitting shareholder's original bank statements; (2) employment contract, payroll records, or dividend distribution documentation evidencing the economic origin of the funds; (3) if the contribution derives from a corporate sale, the stamped sale-and-purchase agreement and tax clearance certificate; (4) a signed Source of Funds (SOF) and Source of Wealth (SOW) declaration, supported by statements; (5) Board Resolution of CY_LTD resolving the share issue and the subscribing shareholder's acceptance; (6) the 12-month capital-expenditure and liquidity plan for the inflight catering kitchen (fit-out of the bonded Larnaca production facility, ovens, blast chillers, trolleys, vehicles), aligning the injected amount to a verifiable commercial purpose; (7) statutory declaration under the Cyprus Oaths Law confirming the funds are free of encumbrances and not derived from criminal activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty sanctions due diligence on airline customers and trading partners: non-EEA state-owned airlines, airlines on enhanced-risk lists, or contracts touching sanctioned Russia/Belarus/Crimea geometry will trigger automatic rejection under EU Regulation 833/2014 and related UN/OFAC regimes; any catering uplift for a sanctioned air carrier is a hard compliance blocker.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed inflight catering agreement with each airline, accompanied by the airline's corporate group chart; (2) a signed sanctions-compliance letter from the airline's legal department confirming that neither the airline nor its UBOs are listed under EU/UN/OFAC sanctions and that no Russian/Ukrainian-disputed route is serviced by the Cyprus kitchen; (3) IATA Operational Safety Audit (IOSA) certificate of the counterparty, considered strong corroborating evidence of institutional compliance; (4) monthly uplift manifest and meal-count reports physically linked to flight numbers, produced by the bonded kitchen and countersigned by the airline's station manager; (5) airport concession evidence from Hermes Airports Ltd confirming ramp-access rights at LCA/PFO; (6) a negative-media/OFAC screening report on the airline generated by sanctions-screening software within 7 days of submission.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-customer concentration and cash-flow visibility: Cyprus bank credit and onboarding committees automatically escalate a newly formed catering company whose entire receivables stream depends on one airline or whose forecast shows lumpy monthly receipts inconsistent with the 'Aviation Contract Wire' and 'Monthly ACH' rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Binding letters of intent (LOIs) or framework agreements with at least two independent air carriers, or a concession award from Hermes Airports Ltd for sole ramp-delivery incumbency; (2) a board-approved 12-month treasury forecast segmented by settlement rail (Aviation Contract Wire vs Monthly ACH/SEPA DD), by air carrier, and by seasonality; (3) a shareholders' liquidity comfort letter pledging up to EUR 150,000 of subordinated liquidity until the kitchen reaches monthly positive operating cash flow; (4) sample invoice set showing B2B VAT treatment (reverse charge or zero-rating for export meals) and correct ISO 3166/IATA flight references; (5) a director's EU bank reference letter in the standard A5 form; (6) kitchen insurance certificates covering product liability and business interruption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory food-business licensing and airport bonded-warehouse permits: banks de-risk entities whose Veterinary Services and Food Safety Directorate license application is pending, unconverted, or deficient; the absence of a valid food establishment registration under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 is a hard blocker for onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Acknowledged license application to the Veterinary Services and Food Safety Directorate of the Cyprus Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment (with filing date stamp); (2) the HACCP food-safety plan of the Larnaca kitehen, validated by an EU-certified food-safety consultant; (3) the food business operator (FBO) registration confirmation by the District Administration Office; (4) the site lease agreement for the bonded production unit at Larnaca airport industrial zone, with a remaining term of not less than 24 months; (5) Cyprus tax registration certificates (Tax Identification Number and VAT registration certificate); (6) food product liability insurance certificate with minimum coverage of EUR 1,000,000; (7) confirmation letters from Hermes Airports Ltd granting airside access and bonded-dispatch parking for meal delivery vehicles.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For EU/EEA shareholders, inbound equity or loan capital is routed exclusively via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) to the CY_LTD EUR IBAN at the Tier-1 operating bank; the ISO 20022 Remittance Information field must state: 'Equity Contribution under Shareholders Agreement dated [DD/MM/YYYY] of CY_LTD' and the debtor bank should classify the transfer as a capital transaction. For non-EEA shareholders, the mandatory rail is SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking; the SWIFT sender field must contain the exact legal name of the shareholder, and Field 70 (Remittance Information) must read 'Share Subscription / Capital Injection under Board Resolution dated [DD/MM/YYYY]'. The receiving Central Bank of Cyprus ITRS classification will be BPM6 code M0A3 (direct investment / equity capital); if the injection is structured as a shareholder loan, the BPM6 code becomes M0A4 (direct investment / other capital) and a signed loan agreement (with arm's-length interest at EURIBOR 3M plus 0.5-2.0%) must be lodged with the bank in advance. Verification protocol: (1) Board Resolution of CY_LTD authorizing the share issue or loan acceptance; (2) updated register of members and share certificates; (3) evidence of remittance from the shareholder's banking account; (4) confirmation of the economic purpose, namely pre-operating fit-out and equipment purchase for the ISIC 5621 airport bonded kitchen; (5) the subscribed capital is released into the Capital Escrow Account and made available T+0 or T+1 upon matching of the inbound SWIFT/SEPA message. Prohibited practices: fragmented small-amount deposits, mixing shareholder funds with trade receipts, and third-party (non-shareholder) remitters; all such patterns trigger additional AMLs inquiry and delay treasury availability by 5-10 business days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from CY_LTD are executed exclusively from the operational EUR account using the following clearing rails: (i) EU/EEA suppliers of raw food, spices, airline meal packaging, disposable cutlery, kitchen consumables, and logistic subcontractors settle by SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) with the ISO 20022 purpose code PURC or TRAD; orders initiated before 14:30 Cyprus time settle on T+0 via TARGET2. (ii) Non-EEA suppliers and international freight forwarders settle by SWIFT MT103; all payments above EUR 25,000 equivalent require the underlying commercial invoice and, where goods are imported under bond, the customs declaration; USD-denominated instructions are subject to OFAC screening at the US correspondent bank, therefore the recipient's legal name and address must exactly match the supplier's banking records. (iii) High-value, high-risk procurement of capital equipment (industrial ovens, blast chillers, refrigerated trolleys, dishwashing lines) is executed through a Documentary Letter of Credit (MT700 / MT707) under UCP600 issued through the Tier-1 bank's Trade Finance unit; the documentary set includes the signed purchase contract, proforma invoice, bill of lading or air waybill, packing list, and certificate of conformity with EU food-safety standards (CE/FDA where applicable). (iv) The 'Monthly ACH' target rail is mapped to the European SEPA Direct Debit Core (SDD) scheme and to monthly SWIFT MT103 batches for airlines' finance departments; when contracting IATA-member air carriers, the dispatch of monthly meal invoices through the IATA Cargo Account Settlement Systems (CASS) or the carrier's proprietary billing portal is permitted, but collections are settled onto the CY_LTD operating account through the Tier-1 bank and not through the EMI wallet. (v) Airport concession fees, ramp lease charges, electricity, water, and waste-disposal invoices from Hermes Airports Ltd and its service companies are paid via SEPA Direct Debit Mandates or one-off SCT payments, with the concession contract number encoded in the remittance information. (vi) Monthly salary payments and Cyprus Social Insurance Fund contributions (GESY and social insurance) are made via bank-initiated batch standing orders in SEPA XML pain.008 format. Every outbound wire must carry a legible purpose description; invoices in a foreign currency are converted at the bank's interbank reference rate plus a pre-agreed margin of 0.2-0.7% for the catering industry, unless covered by an FX forward contract, and the bank requires that the designated treasury signatory pre-approves every single payment above EUR 10,000 in the host-to-host channel.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Outright Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, EUR/TRY): permitted for maturities between 1 week and 24 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 (Cyprus) agreement with the relationship bank; the bank requires documentation of the underlying operational exposure through a 12-month forecasting model of airline contract-wire inflows; no Central Bank approval is required, but each trade is reportable to an EU trade repository under EMIR Refit unless intra-group exemption applies.

FX Swaps (EUR against USD/GBP/CHF): permitted for temporary liquidity transformation around the monthly airline invoicing cycle (e.g., receiving USD receivables and swapping to EUR for payroll and supplier payments) with maturities up to 12 months; physically settled FX swaps are outside the EMIR clearing obligation but remain subject to transaction-level reporting; a signed ISDA/CSA and a dedicated treasury credit line with the Tier-1 bank are mandatory prerequisites.

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS): permitted where a shareholder loan or aircraft-ancillary financing is denominated in USD or GBP and CY_LTD's functional currency is EUR; maturity aligned to the underlying loan amortization schedule under an ISDA 2002 (Cyprus) master agreement; subject to both the internal credit committee limit and the standard EMIR reporting/trade repository obligations.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): permissible only for exotic and non-convertible currencies (e.g., EUR/TRY, EUR/EGP, EUR/NAD) through the Cyprus bank's global markets desk, which screens back-to-back with its London or New York branch; NDFs are not available for Eurozone currencies and are not recommended for the predominant USD/EUR risk of the catering business; physical delivery forwards are preferred for all fully convertible pairs.

FX Options (OTC call/put on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP): permitted when purchased (premium paid upfront) from the Tier-1 bank's options desk; selling or writing options by CY_LTD requires an enhanced internal treasury mandate and documented end-user hedging justification under EMIR; conservative practice restricts option usage to hedging of confirmed airline catering contract receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Republic of Cyprus
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty per month; continued default beyond 3 months exposes the company to administrative strike-off and court-imposed fines on directors on the basis of the Companies Law, Cap. 113.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Republic of Cyprus
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid levy incurs automatic 10% late fee; repeated non-payment is a statutory ground for strike-off and blocks issuance of certificates of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June following the calendar year end (6 months after 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic fine for late filing, default interest at 5% per annum, late-payment surcharge, and criminal quantum for fraudulent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Confirmation (Form UBO Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the Annual Return by the incorporation anniversary plus 42 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing inaccurate UBO information constitutes a criminal offence subject to fines up to EUR 20,000 and persistent default supports strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Cyprus companies are audited unless the audit exemption applies: gross assets do not exceed EUR 350,000 and annual gross turnover does not exceed EUR 70,000. The company must not be part of a group and must not be a regulated entity. Inflight catering operations with material turnover therefore trigger an obligatory independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the EU, with IFRS for SMEs permitted for eligible private entities; consolidated financial statements must apply full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must file an annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation with the Registrar of Companies at the same time as its statutory Annual Return, verifying that the data in the central Beneficial Ownership Register is accurate. Any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 14 days of occurrence.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Directors' and Members' Meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat rate (Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002); Cyprus-resident companies taxed on worldwide income; non-resident companies taxed only on Cyprus-source income attributable to a Cyprus permanent establishment.
